messages:
alex: Heads-up — after last night's kernel-chooser tweak we started seeing a spike in OOMs on our p4d-medium fleet (~8 GPUs) for long-seq Chat workloads. Error sample: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating workspace 324MB (requested by FlashAttentionKernel v2)
```
Logs show FlashAttention being chosen for batches where previously we fell back to Triton cuBLAS path. Rolling back avoids the OOMs.

maria: Thanks. Do we have a perf profile showing why chooser picked FA? My guess: new heuristic prefers FA for slightly larger batch*seq that now appears because of changed batching heuristics. Can you paste the sample distribution?

kai: I pulled a 30m trace from canary group (`nsys` + runtime traces). Seq_len P50=512, P95=1024, P99=1536. Batch size distribution is a bit bimodal because of KV-cache reuse collisions — some requests reuse large KV and get grouped. FA workspace scales ~O(batch*seq) and the chooser wasn't accounting for cached-kv residency.

alex: Right. Here's the kernel chooser log for one OOM request: `chosen=FlashAttentionV2 required_ws=360MB available=320MB fallback=TritonMatmul` — chooser still picks FA because `perf_score` favored it (lower latency in microbench for that shape). We didn't factor in transient mem pressure from KV cache slices.

maria: Quick repro script I used: 
```
# simulate workload mix
run_eval --model llama-13b --seq=1536 --batch=2 --kv-resident=avg
```
`nsys` shows allocator fragmentation spikes right before OOM. cublasLt path uses a temporary workspace pool that gets reclaimed more aggressively; FA's workspace comes from the slab and fails.

taylor: Two short mitigations we can ship today: 1) Enforce an upper `workspace_cap` per-GPU (config in runtime) that causes chooser to pick fallback if required_ws > cap; 2) Add KV-aware headroom: reduce effective available by max_reserved_kv (per-cust metric) when deciding.

alex: Proposed chooser pseudo: 
```
if required_ws > workspace_cap: choose(fallback)
elif required_ws > available_memory - kv_reserved: choose(fallback)
else: choose(best_latency)
```
Cap suggestion: set `workspace_cap` = 0.8 * slab_free_at_start for p4d-medium then tune.

kai: Also recommend collecting `seq_len` histogram and `kv_delta` per-request so we can compute a safe cap dynamically: cap = percentile(required_ws, 99.5) * 1.05 per shape bucket. That avoids one-size-fits-all.

maria: I ran quick perf impact sim: forcing fallback for shapes above 300MB workspace increases p50 latency by ~4% but reduces OOM rate to 0 in 1k sample. Acceptable trade for now.

runtime-bot: incident.alert: OOMs on p4d-medium group increased by +210% (last 1h). Canary rollback in progress? :warning:

alex: I'm going to push a guarded change to chooser that adds `workspace_cap` + kv-aware headroom behind a feature flag. Plan: canary 5% for 1h, monitor OOMs and tail latency. If stable, ramp to 25% over 2h. Rollback on OOM > baseline or tail latency +20%.

taylor: Add instrumentation: emit `chosen_kernel, required_ws, slab_free, kv_reserved, batch, seq` to token-level telemetry so we can later run offline analysis. Also create an alert on chooser-fallback-rate spike (indicates cap too low).

kai: I'll add the histogram collector + small job to compute per-shape 99.5p `required_ws` nightly. We can bake that into a candidate `workspace_cap` config automatically.

maria: Test checklist before canary: unit for chooser boolean gate, integration repro job, nsys profile on canary sample, and a quick run with max-KV stress. I've added tasks in the runbook.

alex: Patch landed to staging under `chooser.workspace_cap_flag` (off by default). Deploying to canary now. Will post telemetry after 15m.

runtime-bot: deploy.event: canary group updated (5% traffic) — chooser.workspace_cap_flag=on :rocket:

alex: Telemetry after 15m: OOMs back to baseline, fallback-rate 12% for the affected shape, p95 latency +6% on that shape only. Looks good so far. Moving to 25% in 30m unless objections.

maria: SGTM. Follow-up items: long-term we should: 1) make kernel microbench include a simulated slab usage signal, 2) implement pre-reserve API for KV so chooser can know exact reservation at scheduling time, 3) consider a tiny FA variant that trades some perf for smaller workspace (quantized soft-fallback).

alex: Agree. Filing a GH epic for follow-ups and add to next retro. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
